title: New NPR Poll: Democrats Hold a Midterm Edge, but the Wave May Be Limited
excerpt: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds Democrats leading the generic congressional ballot by 10 points among registered voters and 8 points among likely voters, one week before Election Day.
content:
A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll released October 27 finds Democrats positioned to gain control of the U.S. House in next week's midterm elections — but with warning signs that any wave may be smaller than the top-line numbers suggest.

The poll, conducted October 19-20 among 1,289 registered voters, found Democrats leading the generic congressional ballot by 10 percentage points among registered voters and 8 points among likely voters. The margin of error was plus or minus 3.7 points for registered voters and 3.8 points for likely voters.

President Donald Trump's job approval stood at 38% among registered voters, with 61% disapproving, and 40% among likely voters, with 59% disapproving. In both groups, 53% said they strongly disapproved — matching the highest level the poll has recorded. His favorability among likely voters was 37% favorable to 59% unfavorable.

The economy dominated voters' concerns. One-third of respondents said they had experienced financial hardship in the past year, and four in 10 said their personal finances had worsened. Preserving democracy resonated with Democrats and independents, while immigration ranked as the top issue for self-described MAGA supporters.

Why the lead may not become a wave

The same poll contains the caveats. Dissatisfaction with the president does not automatically translate into support for Democratic candidates, the survey's analysts note. Redistricting since the 2020 Census, including mid-decade redistricting in Republican-controlled states, has tilted congressional seats in Republicans' favor nationally. And Democratic voters themselves sound nervous: 81% of Democratic likely voters said they believed the Democratic candidate in their district would win, compared with 98% who said they would vote Democratic — a 17-point gap researchers flagged as notable nervousness.

The Senate, meanwhile, remains far harder for Democrats to capture, and analysts quoted in coverage of the poll caution that close races may not be decided on election night — a normal feature of vote counting, not a sign of a problem.

What it means here

Webb County voters are already deciding. More than 26,000 ballots were cast in the first week of early voting in Webb County, according to KGNS, and early voting runs through October 30, with Election Day on November 3. The local ballot includes the Laredo mayor's race, city council seats, and the TX-28 congressional race — contests where national winds matter less than who shows up. A poll is a snapshot of the country, not a prediction about Webb County. The only number that counts here is the one the county elections office reports after the polls close.
